title: Token Playback & Scrubber — UX notes and backlog
content:
Objective:

Build a small, focused UX flow for a "Token Playback" view: a scrubber + timeline that lets engineers replay a single invocation at token granularity to understand how cost and latency accumulate and where hotspots occur. This is intended as a diagnostic complement to the existing per-invocation waterfall — targeted at quick root-cause and hypothesis validation (did quantization cause a spike? cache miss? kernel fallback?).

Why a playback view (problem statement):
- Waterfalls and traces show aggregated spans but are hard to reason about the temporal ordering of token generation vs. kernel/hardware events.
- Teams repeatedly ask for a way to step through a request one token at a time and surface the associated micro-cost (GPU kernel time), api-layer latency, batch-level waits, and cache hits.
- Current token inspectors list tokens and costs but lack a temporal scrubber and live mapping to underlying runtime events.

High-level concept:
- Left: compact token rail (scrollable horizontally) showing tokens with color-coded overlays: latency bucket (fast/medium/slow), cost-per-token intensity (heat), generation outcome (str/stop/func).
- Center: timeline playback with scrubber handle — when you drag the handle, a vertical marker moves through the token rail and updates panes. Playback speed controls and single-step/back/forward buttons.
- Right/top: per-token detail card showing: token text, token index, token timestamp, delta-to-prev-token, kernel name, GPU id, batch-id, model-variant (quantized/FP16), cache_hit boolean, token cost contribution (estimated), and a tiny sparkline for downstream token latency trend.
- Bottom: ephemeral mini-waterfall focused on the last N ms around current token (to show host vs. device time split), and an event list (kernel start/stop, cache operations, routing fallback).

Wireframe iteration notes (v0 -> v2):
- v0: simple horizontal token rail + timeline marker. Clicking tokens updates detail card. Basic heatmap overlay for cost.
- v1: add playback controls, per-token kernel/hardware mapping, hover tooltips with links to the trace span in the global Trace Viewer. Add ability to collapse tokens into "phrases" (e.g., system/prompt/assistant) for jumping.
- v2: include diff mode (compare two invocations side-by-side using the same timeline), introduce an annotations layer where users can pin notes to tokens, and integrate a quick "create ticket" that attaches a screenshot + trace id.

Interaction patterns and microcopy: 
- Scrubber tooltip: "Dragging shows token-level events; press space to play"
- Step buttons: Back (◀ 1 token), Play/Pause, Forward (1 token ▶)
- Cost hover: "Estimated unit cost: $0.00012 — derived from kernel time + model slice"
- Cache hit indicator: green check + hover: "KV cache hit — token served from KV cache (no model kernel)"

Data & backend signals required (minimal set):
- per_token: token_text, token_index, timestamp_ms, delta_ms, token_cost_estimate (float), cache_hit (bool), kernel_id, kernel_name, device_id, batch_id, model_variant, token_role (user/system/assistant), generation_status (streamed/complete/stop).
- span_events: ordered list of runtime events with timestamps tied to token indices (kernel_start/stop, kv_fetch_start/stop, routing_decision).
- trace_id or invocation_id to link back to full trace.
- retention note: playback needs higher-resolution timestamps — request 90-day high-res retention for traces used by playback (opt-in).

Edge cases & performance constraints: 
- Very long responses (>2k tokens): default to an aggregated view with phrase buckets and allow manual "expand around marker".
- Missing kernel mapping for older invocations: fallback to showing token-level latencies but mark hardware fields as "unknown".
- Streaming partials: when the invocation is ongoing or incomplete, allow playback of completed prefix only and grey out future tokens.

Accessibility & mobile: 
- Scrubber handles must be reachable via keyboard (arrow keys = single-step).
- Color palette: avoid red/green dependence; use hue+pattern for heatmap for colorblind accessibility.
- Mobile: simplified view — token list vertical + tap to expand token detail, no continuous playback (resource-heavy), but allow single-step forward/back.

Hypotheses to validate in usability tests: 
- H1: Engineers can identify the top root cause (kernel vs host vs cache) of a token spike in under 90s with the playback view.
- H2: The scrubber reduces context-switching (between Trace Viewer and Token Inspector) by 50% for common debugging flows.
- H3: Diff mode clarifies regressions caused by model variant/quant changes faster than manual comparison.

Open questions (notes to self):
- Should we display monetary cost by default or hide behind an experimental flag? (privacy/contractors/enterprise concerns).
- Where do we store user annotations (customer-owned, or in Redwoods' metadata store)?
- What is the canonical mapping from kernel time to token cost? Should we surface both raw kernel time and normalized token-cost?

Backlog (prioritized):
- P0: Implement minimal token rail + scrubber + per-token detail card (backend contract + API for per_token + span_events). Acceptance: load invocation < 3s for up to 512 tokens.
- P0: Playback step controls + keyboard accessibility. Acceptance: keyboard step works on mac/windows and mobile tap fallback.
- P1: Heatmap overlays (cost intensity) and cache_hit badges. Acceptance: hover shows cost breakdown and cache evidence.
- P1: Link-through to Trace Viewer and to specific kernel spans. Acceptance: clicking trace link opens trace at approximate timestamp.
- P2: Diff mode (two invocations side-by-side). Acceptance: synchronize scrubbers and highlight token mismatch.
- P2: Annotation pins + create-ticket export (attach trace and screenshot).
- Tech spike: retention + storage cost estimate for high-resolution per-token traces for 90 days.

Acceptance criteria (detailed for P0):
- UI: Scrubber renders tokens horizontally, draggable marker updates right-hand detail card in < 150ms.
- Backend: per_token API returns for 95% of calls in < 200ms for 512-token payloads.
- UX: In internal usability test with 6 engineers, 5/6 complete the identification task in < 2 minutes.

Mockups & implementation notes: 
- Figma frames in linked_artifacts show layout grid: token rail height 80px, token pill min width 28px, timeline full width.
- Use existing Token Inspector styles (reuse color tokens) but add small icons for kernel/device.
- Defer mobile-first redesign; start desktop web.

Next steps / meeting plan: 
- Sync with Kai (runtime) to finalize kernel/trace contract by 2025-03-04.
- Run backend cost spike estimation with infra (SLA) — Devon to produce estimate by 2025-03-10.
- Quick usability testing session with 6 frontend/backend engineers (internal) — schedule week of 2025-03-17.

Notes / informal brain-dump: 
- Would be really nice to show "estimated per-token energy" but that is out-of-scope for MVP.
- Consider a keyboard-driven mode where you can type a token index and jump — handy for long transcripts.
- Think about saving a "playback view" snapshot that can be mutated and shared with teammates (debug snapshots).

References and similar patterns seen elsewhere: 
- Video scrubbers and devtools timeline (browser devtools performance flame chart) are strong analogies.
- Some APM products provide step-by-step request playback; we can borrow interaction affordances (playback speed, step-by-step).

Status: draft -> moving to in_review once kernel contract confirmed.

End of notes.
